title: Loco Translate Troubleshooting
description: Fix missing translations, overwritten .po files, plugin update wiping strings, and incorrect locale loading.

steps.title: Identify Untranslated Scope
steps.instructions: Note whether strings are missing site-wide, for one plugin/theme only, or in admin vs front end. Confirm the active site language under Settings → General.

steps.title: Use Custom Save Location (Not Author Directories)
steps.instructions: Save translations to wp-content/languages/loco/ — not inside plugin or theme folders. Author directories are overwritten on plugin/theme updates.

steps.title: Sync Template After Plugin Updates
steps.instructions: After a plugin update, open the bundle in Loco → Sync to pull new source strings. Re-translate added or changed strings and save the .po/.mo files.

steps.title: Recompile and Verify .mo Files
steps.instructions: Loco auto-compiles .mo on save. If translations still missing, delete the .mo and re-save the .po. Confirm file permissions allow the web server to read them.

steps.title: Confirm Correct Text Domain and Locale
steps.instructions: Translate the right bundle (plugin slug text domain). Verify locale code matches WordPress (e.g. de_DE not de). Check for duplicate .mo files loading the wrong one.

steps.title: Clear Caches and Object Cache
steps.instructions: Page cache and persistent object cache can serve stale translated pages. Purge all caches after saving translations and test in a private browser window.

steps.title: Handle JavaScript (Jed/JSON) Translations
steps.instructions: Block editor and some plugins use JSON translation files. Use Loco's JSON tab or regenerate script translations if admin UI strings stay in English.

steps.title: Verify Translations on Front End and Admin
steps.instructions: Spot-check key plugin strings, menus, and WooCommerce/checkout labels in the target language. Document custom Loco path for future deploys.
